name: Embeddings and Generative Models
strandNote: Not needed for the quant path. Machine learning research roles, and reading papers on embeddings and generative models.
description: Learn vectors that stand for things, squeeze data through a bottleneck, generate new points, and pass messages on a graph.

requires.why: Similarity is the cosine of the angle between two vectors, from l3.
Embeddings were first trained there as a lookup table; this level studies them.
Embeddings are trained with the NumPy array autograd built in that level.
A linear autoencoder spans the top principal components of l11.
Autoencoders are trained with the optimisers of that level.
The ELBO is built from KL divergence, which is at least 0 by Jensen there.
Sampling z as mu plus sigma times noise is the recipe of l16.
One message-passing step is a random-walk step on the network, from l14.
Many layers smooth every node alike, as repeated multiplication settles in l4.
A graph network is trained with the optimisers of that level.

lessonObjectives.l1-a-table-of-vectors: Explain an embedding as a table of vectors, and a one-hot product as a row lookup.
lessonObjectives.l2-cosine-similarity: Write cosine similarity for a whole table at once, and say why length is divided out.
lessonObjectives.l3-nearest-in-the-space: Find nearest neighbours in an embedding space, and judge whether they make sense.
lessonObjectives.l4-embedding-stocks: Build stock embeddings from return co-movement, and compare them with sector labels.
lessonObjectives.l5-squeeze-and-rebuild: Build an autoencoder with a bottleneck, and read its reconstruction error.
lessonObjectives.l6-linear-autoencoder-is-pca: Show that a trained linear autoencoder spans the top principal components.
lessonObjectives.l7-a-curved-bottleneck: Train a nonlinear autoencoder that beats PCA on curved data at the same size.
lessonObjectives.l8-odd-days: Use reconstruction error to flag unusual days, and choose a threshold on held-out data.
lessonObjectives.l9-a-hidden-cause: Write a latent variable model as a story, and sample data from it.
lessonObjectives.l10-the-elbo: Derive the evidence lower bound with Jensen's inequality, and name its two terms.
lessonObjectives.l11-gaussian-kl: Derive the KL divergence between a normal and the standard normal, and check it numerically.
lessonObjectives.l12-reparameterisation: Write the reparameterisation trick, and train a small VAE on two-dimensional data.
lessonObjectives.l13-adding-noise: Derive the closed form for a point after many noising steps, and compute it for a schedule.
lessonObjectives.l14-predict-the-noise: Train a small network to predict the noise added to two-dimensional points.
lessonObjectives.l15-sampling-backwards: Write the reverse sampling loop, and check its samples against the data.
lessonObjectives.l16-the-schedule: Explain how the noise schedule and the number of steps change the samples.
lessonObjectives.l17-graphs-as-matrices: Write a graph as adjacency and degree matrices, and build the normalised adjacency.
lessonObjectives.l18-passing-messages: Explain one message-passing step as a random-walk step on the graph.
lessonObjectives.l19-a-gcn-layer: Write a graph convolution layer, and check it against a loop over neighbours.
lessonObjectives.l20-labels-on-a-graph: Train a graph network to label nodes from a few known labels, and see deep layers over-smooth.
